claims.text: Increasing yttrium concentration in a multiprincipal-element alloy will promote formation of a continuous, adherent protective oxide scale.
Optimizing yttrium partitioning will promote formation of a continuous, adherent protective oxide scale.
The protective scale will primarily consist of Al2O3.
Fine Y2O3 particles will reinforce the scale at oxide grain boundaries.
The yttrium-modified scale suppresses oxygen ingress and outward metal-ion diffusion.
Suppressing transport through the scale enhances oxidation resistance and preserves high-temperature material integrity.
Laser-cladding-induced nanocrystalline refinement provides grain-boundary diffusion paths for Al and Cr that accelerate formation of a continuous protective scale.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles physically pin the scale and reduce diffusion paths.
Yttrium segregates to Al2O3 grain boundaries during oxidation.
Yttrium at oxide grain boundaries inhibits outward diffusion of metal cations.
Yttrium at oxide grain boundaries inhibits inward oxygen diffusion.
Yttrium promotes rapid nucleation and growth of a protective Al2O3 scale.
Y-containing oxide pinning and improved interfacial bonding reduce scale spallation during thermal cycling.
Higher-yttrium samples will have thinner, more compact, and more adherent oxide scales than the nominal-yttrium baseline.
Higher-yttrium samples will exhibit lower oxidation rates, measured by reduced weight gain.
Higher-yttrium samples will exhibit superior mechanical stability during thermal cycling.
The nominal-yttrium baseline tends to form a thicker, more porous, and less adherent oxide layer.
The hypothesized behavior should hold from 900°C to 1000°C for exposures up to 120 hours.
Alloy chemistry and processing-induced nanocrystalline structure can act synergistically in governing oxidation performance.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says yttrium promotes rapid growth of Al2O3, whereas the predicted outcome requires a thinner scale and lower oxidation rate. Rapid nucleation could coexist with slower subsequent growth, but that distinction is not stated.

The initial state is conventionally processed and the intervention includes laser cladding to alter partitioning and microstructure, but the falsification design gives both groups identical processing and comparable nanocrystalline structures. Thus the experiment isolates yttrium concentration but does not test the proposed processing or partitioning intervention against the stated conventional baseline.

The intervention is disjunctive—higher yttrium concentration and/or optimized partitioning—while the stated null result from a concentration comparison is claimed to falsify the entire hypothesis. Such a result would not independently falsify the partitioning branch.
